messages:
jess: Heads up — after the infra refactor I just ran a deploy and the analytics uploader SA isn't picking up the IRSA role. App started failing with 403s to S3. Looks like SA annotation might be wrong or the SA landed in the wrong namespace. Anyone seen this pattern recently?
ankur: Ugh. Did terraform create the SA or did the helm chart?
jess: TF module created it (modules/k8s-serviceacct). The module uses a namespace var, but the plan showed namespace as \"\" for that resource before apply (I think defaulting to default ns). Plan output snippet: 
``` 
# module.analytics.module.sa.aws_eks_service_account.analytics[0] will be created
+ resource \"kubernetes_service_account\" \"analytics\" {
    + metadata {
        + name      = \"analytics-uploader\"
        + namespace = \"\"
        + annotations = {
            + (known after apply) = \"\"
          }
      }
  }
```
ankur: That explains namespace mismatch. If SA ended up in default ns the IRSA annotation won't match the role binding in analytics ns. Also worth checking the annotation itself — I remember a bug where a leading space in the ARN breaks the EKS controller.
lina: I pulled the SA from cluster: `kubectl get sa analytics-uploader -A -o yaml` and saw this in default ns: 
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: analytics-uploader
  namespace: default
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: \" arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/rdw-analytics-uploader\"
```
lina: note the leading space before arn. That'll stop the OIDC controller from matching.
jess: Nice catch. So two issues: namespace variable empty in TF module usage, and accidental whitespace in the ARN template. Where would the space come from? probably the outputs/var concat in the role module.
ankur: Quickly: we can patch the SA in-cluster to restore immediate functionality, then fix TF vars+module and re-apply. Commands: 
```
kubectl -n default patch serviceaccount analytics-uploader --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/metadata/annotations/eks.amazonaws.com~1role-arn","value":"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/rdw-analytics-uploader"}]'
kubectl -n default get sa analytics-uploader -o yaml | sed -n '1,60p'
```
ankur: Then either `terraform import kubernetes_service_account.analytics \"analytics/analytics-uploader\"` into the module, or delete the SA and let TF recreate in the correct ns after fixing vars.
jess: I'll patch now to stop the immediate 403s, then open a PR to ensure the module requires namespace non-empty and trims annotation strings.
infra-bot: terraform plan finished for branch jess/analytics-sa-fix — 1 to change, 0 to add, 0 to destroy :white_check_mark:
lina: If you need a quick guard I can add a `validation` block in the module var for namespace so empty string fails early. Also add `trimspace(var.role_arn)` in the interpolation.
jess: Perfect. I'll do the patch + PR, then put a note in CHANGELOG. @ankur can you handle the terraform import or recreate after PR merges?
ankur: Yep, I'll handle the import during the maintenance window tonight. Will also run `kubectl get rolebinding -n analytics -o yaml` after to ensure rolebinding targets the correct SA name/namespace.
jess: Thanks all. Posting PR link once up. :thumbsup:
